"'''(Everything I Do) I Do It for You'''" is a song by Canadian singer-songwriter [[Bryan Adams]]. Written by Adams, [[Michael Kamen]], and [[Robert John "Mutt" Lange]], the [[power ballad]] was the lead single for both the [[Robin Hood: Prince of Thieves#Music|soundtrack album]] from the 1991 film ''[[Robin Hood: Prince of Thieves]]'' and Adams' sixth studio album, ''[[Waking Up the Neighbours]]'' (1991). The single was released on June 17, 1991, by [[A&M Records]] and the accompanying music video was directed by [[Julien Temple]].

The song was a chart success internationally, reaching the number-one position on the music charts of at least 19 countries. In the United Kingdom, it spent 16 consecutive weeks at number one on the [[UK Singles Chart]]. It went on to sell more than 15 million copies worldwide, making it Adams' most successful song and one of the [[List of best-selling singles|best-selling singles]] of all time.<ref>{{cite news|title=Review/Pop; Bryan Adams, More Mr. Nice Guy|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1994/03/08/arts/review-pop-bryan-adams-more-mr-nice-guy.html|last=Pareles|first=Jon|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=March 8, 1994|access-date=February 20, 2014|archive-date=May 26, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150526102330/http://www.nytimes.com/1994/03/08/arts/review-pop-bryan-adams-more-mr-nice-guy.html|url-status=live}}</ref> The song has been covered by hundreds of singers and artists around the world.

"(Everything I Do) I Do It for You" is a song by Canadian singer-songwriter Bryan Adams. Written by Adams, Michael Kamen, and Robert John "Mutt" Lange, the power ballad was the lead single for both the soundtrack album from the 1991 film Robin Hood: Prince of Thieves and Adams' sixth studio album, Waking Up the Neighbours (1991). The single was released on June 17, 1991, by A&M Records and the accompanying music video was directed by Julien Temple.

The song was a chart success internationally, reaching the number-one position on the music charts of at least 19 countries. In the United Kingdom, it spent 16 consecutive weeks at number one on the UK Singles Chart. It went on to sell more than 15 million copies worldwide, making it Adams' most successful song and one of the best-selling singles of all time. The song has been covered by hundreds of singers and artists around the world.

sections.heading: Commercial performance
sections.wikitext:
In the United Kingdom, "(Everything I Do) I Do It for You" had the longest unbroken run at number one, spending sixteen consecutive weeks at the top of the [[UK Singles Chart]] from July 7, 1991, to October 27 when it dropped to number four,<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.officialcharts.com/search/singles/(everything%20i%20do)%20i%20do%20it%20for%20you/ |title= (Everything I do) I do it for you in Official Charts |website= [[Official Charts Company|Official Charts]] |access-date= March 19, 2017 |archive-date= February 12, 2017 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20170212093244/http://www.officialcharts.com/search/singles/(everything%20i%20do)%20i%20do%20it%20for%20you/ |url-status= live }}</ref> surpassing the record 11 weeks set by [[Slim Whitman]]'s hit single "[[Rose Marie (song)|Rose Marie]]" in 1955.<ref>{{Cite magazine|date=October 5, 1991|title=Adams Single Breaks No. 1 Longevity Record On U.K. Chart|last=White|first=Adam|url=https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Billboard/90s/1991/BB-1991-10-05.pdf|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|page=4|access-date=February 5, 2024}}</ref> Adams' achievement was celebrated by Whitman in November 1991, when he joined Adams on stage at Wembley Arena to sing "Rose Marie", after which he presented Adams with a plaque commemorating the achievement.<ref>{{cite web|title=Slim Whitman: One of the biggest-selling musicians in the history of country and western|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/slim-whitman-one-of-the-biggestselling-musicians-in-the-history-of-country-and-western-8665780.html|website=Independent|date=19 June 2013|access-date=13 May 2024}}</ref> "(Everything I Do) I Do It for You" also topped the Europe-wide sales chart for eighteen continuous weeks, still an all-time record, and topped the European-wide radio airplay chart for ten weeks.<ref>"European Airplay Top 50" (PDF). Music & Media. 3 August 1991. Retrieved 31 July 2019.</ref>

In the United States, the [[power ballad]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/movies/24-of-the-biggest-and-best-movie-power-ballads/|title=24 of the Biggest and Best Movie Power Ballads|date=November 4, 2016|website=Den of Geek|access-date=March 17, 2021|archive-date=November 20, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201120204310/https://www.denofgeek.com/movies/24-of-the-biggest-and-best-movie-power-ballads/|url-status=live}}</ref> spent seven weeks at number one on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], which combines radio airplay and sales, the longest running number one song since 1983, and seventeen consecutive weeks at number one on the sales-only chart, which at the time set the all-time record for consecutive weeks at one.<ref name="Sandiford-Waller 83">{{cite magazine|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ygkEAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA83|title=Hot 100 Singles Spotlight|last=Sandiford-Waller|first=Theda|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|publisher=BPI Communications Inc.|date=November 9, 1996|access-date=February 26, 2015|page=83|issn=0006-2510|volume=108|number=45|archive-date=November 1, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151101193338/https://books.google.com/books?id=ygkEAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA83|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Billboard'' ranked it as the number-one pop song for 1991.<ref name="usye"/> It also held the number one spot on the US Adult Contemporary Chart for eight consecutive weeks, the longest run atop that chart since 1979, and was the number one song of the year on that chart.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Joel Whitburn's Top Adult Contemporary, 1961–2001|first=Joel|last=Whitburn|publisher=Record Research Incorporated|date=2002|isbn=978-0-89820-149-9|pages=345–348}}</ref>

"(Everything I Do) I Do It for You" also spent nine weeks atop the [[RPM (magazine)|singles chart]] in Adams' native Canada,<ref name="can"/> eleven weeks atop the [[Australian Singles Chart]], and twelve weeks atop the Sweden Singles Chart. In most of the countries where it ascended to number one, it was the number one song for the year 1991, exceptions being Germany (number two), Austria (number two) and Switzerland (number three).
sections.text:
In the United Kingdom, "(Everything I Do) I Do It for You" had the longest unbroken run at number one, spending sixteen consecutive weeks at the top of the UK Singles Chart from July 7, 1991, to October 27 when it dropped to number four, surpassing the record 11 weeks set by Slim Whitman's hit single "Rose Marie" in 1955. Adams' achievement was celebrated by Whitman in November 1991, when he joined Adams on stage at Wembley Arena to sing "Rose Marie", after which he presented Adams with a plaque commemorating the achievement. "(Everything I Do) I Do It for You" also topped the Europe-wide sales chart for eighteen continuous weeks, still an all-time record, and topped the European-wide radio airplay chart for ten weeks.

In the United States, the power ballad spent seven weeks at number one on the Billboard Hot 100, which combines radio airplay and sales, the longest running number one song since 1983, and seventeen consecutive weeks at number one on the sales-only chart, which at the time set the all-time record for consecutive weeks at one. Billboard ranked it as the number-one pop song for 1991. It also held the number one spot on the US Adult Contemporary Chart for eight consecutive weeks, the longest run atop that chart since 1979, and was the number one song of the year on that chart.

"(Everything I Do) I Do It for You" also spent nine weeks atop the singles chart in Adams' native Canada, eleven weeks atop the Australian Singles Chart, and twelve weeks atop the Sweden Singles Chart. In most of the countries where it ascended to number one, it was the number one song for the year 1991, exceptions being Germany (number two), Austria (number two) and Switzerland (number three).

sections.heading: Music videos
sections.wikitext: The official music video for the song was directed by British film, documentary and music video director [[Julien Temple]].<ref name="mvdbase">{{cite web|url=http://www.mvdbase.com/video.php?id=695|title=mvdbase.com – Bryan Adams – "(Everything I do) I do it for you [version 1: concept]"|work=Music Video DataBase|last=Garcia|first=Alex S|access-date=November 2, 2015|archive-date=March 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304075616/http://www.mvdbase.com/video.php?id=695}}</ref> It shows Adams and his band performing the song in a forest with a silk mill in the background, and Adams alone performing on a rocky beachside, intercut with scenes from ''Robin Hood: Prince of Thieves''. The video was filmed in a forest with a derelict silk mill near [[Holford]] in the [[Quantock Hills]] and on a beach with geological cliff formations near [[Kilve]], [[Somerset]], [[England]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sites.google.com/site/saveholfordsilkmills/home/bryan-adams|title=Bryan Adams at The Silk Mills Holford – Holford Silk Mills Holford Somerset|website=sites.google.com|access-date=September 9, 2021|archive-date=September 9, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210909053444/https://sites.google.com/site/saveholfordsilkmills/home/bryan-adams|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://afamilydayout.co.uk/quantock/|title=Four family walks in the Quantock Hills, Somerset|date=November 22, 2016|publisher=Afamilydayout.co.uk|access-date=September 9, 2021|archive-date=September 9, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210909053446/https://afamilydayout.co.uk/quantock/|url-status=live}}</ref> A video was also commissioned for a [[concert|live version]] of the song, directed by [[Andy Morahan]].<ref name="mvdbase2">{{cite web|url=http://www.mvdbase.com/video.php?id=702|title=mvdbase.com – Bryan Adams – "(Everything I do) I do it for you [version 2: live]"|work=Music Video DataBase|last=Garcia|first=Alex S|access-date=November 2, 2015|archive-date=March 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304055415/http://www.mvdbase.com/video.php?id=702}}</ref>
sections.text: The official music video for the song was directed by British film, documentary and music video director Julien Temple. It shows Adams and his band performing the song in a forest with a silk mill in the background, and Adams alone performing on a rocky beachside, intercut with scenes from Robin Hood: Prince of Thieves. The video was filmed in a forest with a derelict silk mill near Holford in the Quantock Hills and on a beach with geological cliff formations near Kilve, Somerset, England. A video was also commissioned for a live version of the song, directed by Andy Morahan.

sections.heading: Awards and accolades
sections.wikitext: Adams, Kamen, and Lange won a [[Grammy Award for Best Song Written for Visual Media|Grammy Award for Best Song Written Specifically for a Motion Picture or Television]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.metrolyrics.com/1992-grammy-awards.html|title=1992 Grammy Awards|publisher=metrolyrics.com|access-date=January 1, 2009|url-status=dead| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090209091440/http://www.metrolyrics.com/1992-grammy-awards.html| archive-date= February 9, 2009}}</ref> and was nominated for the [[Grammy Award for Record of the Year]] at the [[34th Annual Grammy Awards|Grammy Awards of 1992]]. It was also nominated for an [[Academy Award for Best Original Song]], but lost to "[[Beauty and the Beast (Disney song)|Beauty and the Beast]]" from the [[Beauty and the Beast (1991 film)|Disney film of the same name]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oscarguy.com/Oscars/Annual/64th/Oscar.html|publisher=oscarguy.com|title=The 64th Academy Awards (1991) Nominees and Winners|access-date=January 1, 2009| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090124051745/http://www.oscarguy.com/Oscars/Annual/64th/Oscar.html| archive-date= January 24, 2009<!--Added by DASHBot-->}}</ref> As recently as July 2020, it placed at number 13 on YouTube's "Most Listened to Rock Countdown", a monthly tally of the most viewed and listened to songs of the rock genre, both in current release and from the past; this was the second highest-ranked song by Adams after "Please Forgive Me" at number 10.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4wLzacltgUQ|title=Top 100 Most Listened Rock Songs in July 2020|via=www.youtube.com|access-date=January 25, 2021|archive-date=February 1, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210201014828/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4wLzacltgUQ|url-status=live}}</ref> The song was placed 18th in a survey of the favourite songs of British readers of the Guinness Book of Records.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.theguardian.com/uk/2002/may/08/2 |title=Full list: Britain's favourite 100 songs |date=May 8, 2002 |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |location=London |access-date=October 9, 2021 |archive-date=January 31, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210131134957/https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2002/may/08/2 |url-status=live }}</ref>
sections.text: Adams, Kamen, and Lange won a Grammy Award for Best Song Written Specifically for a Motion Picture or Television, and was nominated for the Grammy Award for Record of the Year at the Grammy Awards of 1992. It was also nominated for an Academy Award for Best Original Song, but lost to "Beauty and the Beast" from the Disney film of the same name. As recently as July 2020, it placed at number 13 on YouTube's "Most Listened to Rock Countdown", a monthly tally of the most viewed and listened to songs of the rock genre, both in current release and from the past; this was the second highest-ranked song by Adams after "Please Forgive Me" at number 10. The song was placed 18th in a survey of the favourite songs of British readers of the Guinness Book of Records.

sections.heading: Fatima Mansions version
sections.wikitext:
The Irish band [[The Fatima Mansions|Fatima Mansions]] released a heavily altered cover of the song as part of an ''[[NME]]'' [[tribute album]] in aid of the [[charitable organization|charity]], the [[Scope (charity)|Spastics Society]].<ref name="fm">{{cite book
| first= David
| last= Roberts
| year= 2006
| title= British Hit Singles & Albums
| edition= 19th
| publisher= Guinness World Records Limited
| location= London
| isbn= 1-904994-10-5
| page= 196}}</ref> The [[single (music)|single]] was a [[A-side and B-side|double A-side]] with the [[Manic Street Preachers]]' version of "[[Suicide Is Painless]]". The single entered the [[UK Singles Chart|UK top ten]] in 1992,<ref name="fm" /> and reached number 12 in the [[Republic of Ireland]].<ref>{{cite web|title=The Irish Charts|url=https://www.irma.ie/search/%2A|website=irishcharts.ie|access-date=8 September 2014|archive-date=June 2, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090602061251/http://www.irishcharts.ie/search/placement|url-status=live}} Search by Artist: Fatima Mansions</ref> However, the Manic Street Preachers song received most of the UK [[radio station|radio]] [[airplay (radio)|airplay]].<ref name="fm" /><ref>Nick Dale, "Fatima Mansions" in Peter Buckley (ed.) ''The Rough Guide To Rock''.London; Rough Guides, 2003 {{ISBN|1-84353-105-4}} (p. 364).</ref>
sections.text: The Irish band Fatima Mansions released a heavily altered cover of the song as part of an NME tribute album in aid of the charity, the Spastics Society. The single was a double A-side with the Manic Street Preachers' version of "Suicide Is Painless". The single entered the UK top ten in 1992, and reached number 12 in the Republic of Ireland. However, the Manic Street Preachers song received most of the UK radio airplay.

American singer [[Brandy Norwood|Brandy]] rerecorded "(Everything I Do) I Do It for You" for the standard version of her second studio album, ''[[Never Say Never (Brandy album)|Never Say Never]]'' (1998). Producer [[David Foster]] reworked the arrangement of the original song, with [[Dean Parks]] playing the [[acoustic guitar]].

In 1999, her [[cover version]] was released as the album's final single on a double A-side with "[[U Don't Know Me (Like U Used To)|U Don't Know Me]]" on the Oceanic music market, where it reached the top 30 of New Zealand's [[Recording Industry Association of New Zealand|RIANZ Singles Chart]]. That same year, she performed the song live at [[VH1 Divas|VH1 Divas Live '99]] alongside [[Faith Hill]].
